title: docs(getting-started): add a getting started guide to react-is doc
body:
This PR is mainly done for providing the getting started. Along the way I had change / tweak a few things (that's why there are other files modified). Amongst the different other changes:
- The sidebar contains the title of the page
- The sidebar is smarter and adapts on the content of the navgroup or the document (if either of them contains only one element, this level is discarded)
- The sidebar is a tad wider

While the content of the getting started is mostly done, I need you:
- can you review the [content itself](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/d26ab3986c9c3b0421291c9db33f7e36cf12746d/docgen/src/gettingstarted.md), make sure I talked every important and I didn't go into too much details for others?
- there is no live examples yet. The getting started of the helper have its samples on codepen, but I'm not sure we want to go this. What do you suggest?

comments.body: By analyzing the blame information on this pull request, we identified @vvo to be a potential reviewer

> there is no live examples yet. The getting started of the helper have its samples on codepen, but I'm not sure we want to go this. What do you suggest?

As for the live examples, we need to have them also for the widget examples (#1238)

One possible solution is to use https://github.com/react-toolbox/react-toolbox/blob/dea14144b8969eca748d4899fb05bc8c52734a31/docs/app/components/preview/index.js (babel-standalone).

Basically we would need to create a small Preview component that would take the code sample (that can be obtained via .innerText on a `<code>` block in DOM) then transform that with babel-standalone, injecting the right context (basically every InstantSearch export) and render it. This is what the react toolbox preview does

What do you think?

I just did the tutorial. I find it easy to follow except that the connector part may come too soon, but this will change. 

Results with the e-commerce data :) 

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/6885378/18954209/2ea91c8c-8652-11e6-8748-0dc98096c6ff.png)

Regarding the live example, it would have been nice to use those we are going to add in storybook. 
We can do that by publishing the storybook and then have en embed iframe using the direct link to a story ?

> We can do that by publishing the storybook and then have en embed iframe using the direct link to a story ?

Yep if it works well then why not and is invisible for the user that we are tricking him a bit ;)

But you will first have to be able to create a working /react/storybook to do so, and make the dev/preview experience OK.
That would be very cool. And it seems less complex than using the stuff from react-toolbox.
